name: sectors
description: Bilateral Nigeria-Australia trade and economic sectors. Two levels: a top-level sector (parent: null) and optional sub-sectors. Signals, opportunities, stakeholders and diaspora expertise tags all classify against these codes. Codes are stable identifiers and must never be renamed; labels may be edited.

sectors.label: Critical Minerals
sectors.description: Minerals essential to energy-transition and advanced-manufacturing supply chains. Australia is a major upstream producer and processor; Nigeria holds significant under-developed deposits and is pursuing domestic beneficiation rather than raw-ore export. The primary hero-thread sector.

sectors.label: Lithium and Battery Materials
sectors.description: Lithium exploration, spodumene concentration, refining to battery-grade chemicals, and downstream cathode and cell materials. Australia is the world's largest spodumene producer and is building domestic refining capacity; Nigeria has confirmed lithium-bearing pegmatites across the Central and North-Central belts and has adopted a policy of licensing conditional on local processing. HERO SECTOR.

sectors.label: Rare Earth Elements
sectors.description: Light and heavy rare earth exploration, separation and magnet-materials processing. Relevant to both parties' supply-chain diversification objectives.

sectors.label: Tantalum, Niobium and Tin
sectors.description: Columbite-tantalite and cassiterite mining and processing, historically significant on the Jos Plateau and a live artisanal-to-formal-sector transition challenge with clear traceability and ESG implications.

sectors.label: Copper, Nickel and Cobalt
sectors.description: Base and battery metals relevant to electrification supply chains, where Australian producers and processing technology providers are internationally active.

sectors.label: Education and Skills
sectors.description: Education services, skills recognition and labour-mobility pathways. Australia's second-largest services export category and a long-standing element of the bilateral relationship. The second hero-thread sector.

sectors.label: Higher Education
sectors.description: University-level study, transnational education, branch campuses, articulation agreements and scholarship programmes between Australian and Nigerian institutions.

sectors.label: Skilled Migration Pathways
sectors.description: Migration pathways for skilled workers: occupation-list alignment, skills assessment and recognition of Nigerian qualifications, employer sponsorship, and the study-to-work-to-residence sequence. HERO SECTOR - paired with CM_LITHIUM in the demo narrative.

sectors.label: Vocational Education and Training
sectors.description: Competency-based technical and vocational training, including Australian VET packages delivered in Nigeria, trainer-of-trainers programmes, and industry-linked training for the resources and processing sectors.

sectors.label: Research Collaboration
sectors.description: Joint research programmes, co-supervision, mobility fellowships and shared research infrastructure, concentrated in minerals science, agriculture and public health.

sectors.label: Qualification and Skills Recognition
sectors.description: Mutual recognition of qualifications and occupational licensing - the practical bottleneck that determines whether a training pipeline actually converts into employment.

sectors.label: Agribusiness and Food Systems
sectors.description: Agricultural production, processing, inputs and food security. Australia is a significant grain supplier to Nigeria and a source of dryland-farming technology relevant to Nigerian conditions.

sectors.label: Grains and Pulses
sectors.description: Wheat, barley, sorghum and pulse trade, storage and milling - the largest established goods-trade channel between the two economies.

sectors.label: Livestock and Animal Genetics
sectors.description: Breeding stock, genetics, animal health, feedlot systems and rangeland management, where Australian expertise in arid and semi-arid systems maps onto northern Nigerian conditions.

sectors.label: Agricultural Technology
sectors.description: Precision agriculture, irrigation technology, post-harvest loss reduction, cold chain and farm-management software.

sectors.label: Mining Equipment, Technology and Services
sectors.description: The METS sector: engineering, geological services, mine planning, processing technology, safety systems, environmental management and mine-site services. A major Australian export capability and the most direct commercial adjacency to Nigeria's minerals ambitions.

sectors.label: Energy
sectors.description: Power generation, transmission, fuels and the energy transition.

sectors.label: Renewable Energy
sectors.description: Utility-scale and distributed solar, wind, storage and mini-grid deployment, including the power supply question that sits underneath any mineral-processing proposition.

sectors.label: Natural Gas and LNG
sectors.description: Gas processing, liquefaction, domestic gas-to-power and industrial gas use. Both countries are significant gas exporters and therefore both partners and competitors.

sectors.label: ICT and Digital Economy
sectors.description: Software, data infrastructure, connectivity, cybersecurity and digital government. Nigeria's technology sector is the largest in Africa by investment volume and a substantial source of the skilled diaspora.

sectors.label: Financial Services
sectors.description: Banking, capital markets, insurance, pensions and trade finance, including the mining-project finance capability concentrated in Australian institutions.

sectors.label: Fintech and Payments
sectors.description: Payments, remittances, digital lending and regulatory technology. Remittance corridors are directly relevant to diaspora engagement policy.

sectors.label: Health and Life Sciences
sectors.description: Health systems, medical technology, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics and health workforce development - the latter closely coupled to skilled-migration policy and to ethical-recruitment concerns.

sectors.label: Infrastructure, Transport and Logistics
sectors.description: Transport corridors, ports, rail, construction, project delivery and the logistics capability that determines whether a resources or agricultural opportunity is commercially viable.

sectors.label: Water Management
sectors.description: Water resource management, irrigation, urban water and sanitation, desalination and catchment governance. Australian expertise in scarce-water management is directly transferable to northern Nigeria and to mine-site water stewardship.

sectors.label: Creative Industries
sectors.description: Screen, music, publishing, fashion and design. Nigeria's screen and music sectors have global reach and are a significant soft-power and cultural-diplomacy asset.

sectors.label: Professional and Business Services
sectors.description: Legal, accounting, standards, certification, engineering consultancy and advisory services that underpin cross-border transactions.

sectors.label: Environment and Climate
sectors.description: Climate adaptation, emissions measurement, land restoration, biodiversity and the environmental and social governance standards that increasingly condition access to minerals offtake agreements.
